correctness.rationale: A fixed point requires y=0 and bx²+d=0, impossible. On a two-cycle the first coordinates move by +t and −t with t>0, so the points can be written with midpoint m and first coordinates m∓t/2. The difference of the two vertical return residuals is 2t((1+b)m−2), and at m=2/(1+b) each residual is −Q(t). This proves an exact bijection; the sign of the concave quadratic's maximum, strict monotonicity for c≥c₀, and the positive-root formula give the counts and the expansion in c₀−c. The two signed Jacobians have lower rows (h∓w, α∓z), giving the trace and determinant and det(I−DF²)=2(1+b)tQ′(t). It vanishes at the double root and is negative at the larger simple root, so that root has a multiplier >1. The strict Schur conditions characterize linear asymptotic stability, not nonlinear behavior on the unit circle or a nondegenerate normal form at every double root. A fresh symbolic reproduction in /workspace/review-checks/two_cycle.py also obtained the rational example's amplitudes 1/2 and 31/2 and the stated Schur signs; the frozen checker was inspected, not run.
